title: fix(scheduler): refresh pod status after patch conflicts
body:

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Refreshes the base pod status used by `PodStatusPatchCall` after a conflict.

  The async scheduler status patch path can execute with a stale pod status snapshot. When the patch hits a conflict, the previous logic retried the same stale patch bytes. In some
  scheduler integration flakes, this caused the scheduler's failure condition update to be lost, and the tests timed out waiting for the expected `PodScheduled=False` condition.

  This PR makes `PodStatusPatchCall` fetch the latest pod after a conflict, verify the UID, recompute the desired status patch from the latest status, and retry from that refreshed
  base.

  Observed flakes:

  - https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-integration-master/2070858106245484544
  - https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-integration-master/2070918762965504000

  Both logs include pod status update conflicts like:

  `Operation cannot be fulfilled on pods "...": the object has been modified`

title: Fix: UpdatePod on untracked terminated pod should mark it as terminated
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When a pod in terminal phase (Failed/Succeeded) is synced for the first time without a terminal runtime cache state, mark it as terminated immediately by setting terminatedAt and finished: true. This prevents the pod from getting stuck in terminating state and blocking pod admission.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #139832

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change:
```release-note
Fixed a bug where calling UpdatePod on an untracked but terminated pod would mark it as terminating instead of terminated, potentially blocking pod admission.

title: api: allow DRA-backed extended resource health status names
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Allows pod status validation to accept ResourceStatus.Name values for DRA-backed extended resources using the scheduler-generated claim recorded in pod.status.extendedResourceClaimStatus.

This prepares the API side first. Kubelet reporting for DRA-backed extended resource health is intentionally deferred to a follow-up release to avoid 1.37 kubelets writing pod status that could be rejected after downgrade to a 1.36 apiserver.

Follow-up: #140060

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

None

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This PR only relaxes validation and documents the accepted status name forms. It does not make kubelet report DRA-backed extended resource health yet.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

  This PR protects shared state in scheduler plugin integration test helpers.

  `ReservePlugin` counters are now guarded by a mutex and read through a snapshot helper. `PermitPlugin` assertions now read `waitingPod`, `rejectingPod`, `allowingPod`, and
  `numPermitCalled` through the existing locked `deepCopy()` helper.

  This avoids unsynchronized reads and writes between the test goroutine and scheduler/plugin goroutines.

title: kubectl apply: fix --dry-run=client failure on existing CustomResourceDefinitions
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`kubectl apply --dry-run=client` fails on an existing CustomResourceDefinition
(and other unstructured resources whose server schema advertises strategic
merge) with the cryptic error:

```
applying patch locally: expected a struct, but received a nil
```

The local-apply path in `patchSimple` builds the strategic-merge patch from the
server's OpenAPI schema but then rebuilt the type for the local merge with
`scheme.Scheme.New(gvk)`. `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` is not in kubectl's
compiled-in scheme so that returns `nil` (the error was discarded), and
`strategicpatch.StrategicMergePatch(current, patch, nil)` produces the error.
Server-side apply is unaffected because the apiserver has the type.

This PR makes the three patch-build paths also return the
`strategicpatch.LookupPatchMeta` they built the patch with and has the
local-apply branch use `StrategicMergePatchUsingLookupPatchMeta` with that
metadata instead of looking the type up in the scheme. The local merge then
reuses the exact schema the patch was built from so CRDs and other
OpenAPI-described unstructured objects take the same path as built-in types.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #139538

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This is a master-only regression in the newer client-side dry-run merge path:
the repro fails on master and on v1.36, but v1.34.1 runs it cleanly.

Added a regression test `TestApplyDryRunClientCustomResourceDefinition` in
`pkg/cmd/apply/apply_test.go`, modeled on `TestApplyDryRunClientMergesWithServerState`.
It wires a captured apiextensions OpenAPI v3 fixture plus a fake REST client
returning an existing CRD, and asserts the manifest label merges in while a
live-only label is preserved (proving the strategic merge ran against server
state, not just echoing the manifest). It fails before this change with the
reported error and passes after; the full `pkg/cmd/...` suite stays green.
Resolving the CRD GVK in the test factory required adding
`apiextensions.k8s.io/v1 customresourcedefinitions` to `testDynamicResources()`
in `pkg/cmd/testing/fake.go` (additive).

This PR was written in part with the assistance of generative AI. I have
reviewed and verified every change myself, including building kubectl and
reproducing the fix end-to-end against a live cluster.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kubectl: `apply --dry-run=client` no longer fails with "expected a struct, but received a nil" when applied to an existing CustomResourceDefinition (or other unstructured resource whose server schema advertises strategic merge).
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs
NONE
```

title: apiserver/pod: preserve DRA status fields when old clients clear them via pods/status
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

When a client that predates the DRA fields (`ResourceClaimStatuses`,
`ExtendedResourceClaimStatus`, `NodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatuses`)
issues a `pods/status` update, those fields are absent from the Pod it
sends back. The apiserver stores the update as-is, effectively clearing
DRA status. On the next termination sync, kubelet has no claim info from
the pod status and logs:

```
unprepare dynamic resources: pod "…": ResourceClaim not created yet
```

This leaves pods permanently stuck in `Terminating`.

**Root cause** (from #139772 discussion): Multus CNI uses
`network-attachment-definition-client` which pins `k8s.io/client-go
v0.29.0` — predating DRA fields. It calls `UpdateStatus` to write an
annotation, but the round-tripped Pod has the DRA fields zeroed.

**Fix**: extend `podStatusStrategy.PrepareForUpdate` to restore all three
DRA-related status fields from the old pod when the incoming update omits
them. This applies to running and terminating pods because the old client
can issue status updates throughout the pod lifecycle. For the two slice
fields, an explicit non-nil empty slice (`[]`) remains an allowed way to
clear the field.

The scheduler's Unreserve path now sends that explicit empty list when it
clears `NodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatuses`; its previous generic status
patch serialized the clear as an omitted field.

`DropDisabledPodFields` runs afterwards and will still strip the fields
when the corresponding feature gate is disabled, so there is no
interaction with the feature gate lifecycle.

This complements the kubelet-side resilience fix in #139845.

## Which issue(s) this PR is related to

Fixes #139772

## Type of change

/kind feature
/sig node
/sig api-machinery
/wg device-management
/triage accepted

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Work around a bug in old clients (e.g. Multus CNI using client-go v0.29)
that clear DRA status fields (ResourceClaimStatuses,
ExtendedResourceClaimStatus, NodeAllocatableResourceClaimStatuses) via
pods/status updates, which could leave pods permanently stuck in
Terminating. The apiserver now preserves these fields when an update
from a client unaware of DRA would otherwise remove them.
```

## Testing

title: proxy/nftables: skip ListAll on incremental syncs to fix O(n) scaling
body:
## What this PR does / why we need it

`syncProxyRules` calls `proxier.nftables.ListAll()` on **every** sync,
including incremental (`fullSync=false`) ones. `ListAll` runs:

```
nft --json --terse list table ip kube-proxy
```

which is O(n) in the number of nftables objects. At 44k Services, a
single incremental sync spent almost all of its time inside `ListAll`,
taking over a minute per sync cycle.

**Root cause**: `ListAll` was used to discover which service chains and
affinity sets were previously committed, so stale ones could be cleaned
up. kube-proxy already maintains committed state for map/set elements
in memory across successful syncs; this PR adds equivalent tracking for
service chains (`committedChains`) and affinity sets
(`committedAffinitySets`).

**Fix**:
- Full syncs still call `ListAll` once to reconcile against the actual
  nftables state (picking up chains from a previous kube-proxy instance).
- Incremental syncs use the committed in-memory state instead.
- `committedChains` / `committedAffinitySets` are updated on the proxier
  after each successful `Run`, and are never stale because `nftables.Run`
  is atomic.
- If an incremental sync is promoted to a full sync (e.g. stale-chain
  deletion fails, line 1137), `ListAll` is still called.

**Measured impact** (from issue comments, testing on Antonio's branch
which used the same approach):
- Incremental sync: ~1 minute → **~1-2 seconds** at 44k Services.

## Which issue(s) this PR is related to

Fixes #139513

## Type of change

/kind bug
/sig network
/area kube-proxy
/triage accepted

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed kube-proxy nftables mode performing an O(n) `nft list table`
operation on every incremental sync. With large numbers of Services
(e.g. 44k), incremental syncs now complete in ~2 seconds instead of
over a minute.
```

## Testing

Added `TestIncrementalSyncSkipsListAll` in `pkg/proxy/nftables/proxier_test.go`
using a `listAllCounter` wrapper that counts `ListAll` invocations:
- Initial full sync must call `ListAll` exactly once.
- Subsequent incremental sync must not call `ListAll`.

Build and vet verified with `GOOS=linux go build` and `GOOS=linux go vet`.

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:

/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR proposes new datastore for HPA controller instead of current bimultimap implementation.

The benchmark results shows promising results.


#### Benchmark results

10,000 HPAs, 100 pods/HPA, 10 namespaces, 96-core machine.

**Throughput (reconciliations/second):**

| Workers | Current (BiMultimap) | Proposed (SelectorStore) | Speedup |
|---------|---------------------|------------------------|---------|
| 50 | 2,635 | 444,671 | 169× |
| 100 | 2,600 | 506,873 | 195× |

Current throughput **degrades** with more workers (increased contention). Proposed throughput **scales** with workers until CPU saturation.

**Contention (100 workers):**

| | Avg lock wait per operation |
|---|---|
| Current | 38.2 ms |
| Proposed | 0.178 ms |
| Reduction | **214×** |

**Memory:**

| | Bytes/HPA (10 namespaces) | Bytes/HPA (100 namespaces) |
|---|---|---|
| Current | 474 | 474 |
| Proposed | 226 | 131 |

**Allocations per operation (100 workers):**

| | Bytes/op | Allocs/op |
|---|---|---|
| Current | 6,148,911 | 71,303 |
| Proposed | 563,203 | 30,100 |

#### Impact

With 100 workers and 15s resync period:

- **Current**: 2,600 ops/s → workers spend 99.7% of time blocked on the mutex. Selector overlap check alone consumes seconds of wall clock per cycle.
- **Proposed**: 500K+ ops/s → selector check becomes negligible.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

#139111

title: Add concurrent worker support to the disruption controller
body: #### What type of PR is this? /kind feature #### What this PR does / why we need it: The disruption controller watches Pod events and enqueues the affected PDBs for sync. It currently processes the disruption workqueue with only one worker, which can become a bottleneck during large bursts of Pod updates. When event processing falls behind, informer [pendingNotifications](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5b7710863fbfabcc92125a5af100ba30861f7c95/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/shared_informer.go#L1258) ring buffer may grow continuously, increasing kube-controller-manager memory usage and potentially causing OOM. This PR adds `--concurrent-disruption-syncs` to make the number of disruption controller workers configurable. The default remains `1` to preserve existing behavior. ----- kube-controller-manager memory usage: ---- Disruption controller podInformer pendingNotifications backlog: ---- kube-controller-manager profiling: #### Which issue(s) this PR is related to: #### Special notes for your reviewer: #### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change? ```release-note Added `--concurrent-disruption-syncs` to kube-controller-manager to configure the number of concurrent disruption controller workers. ``` #### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.: ```docs NONE ```

title: Migrate Deployment and ReplicaSet Selector to declarative immutable validation
body:
## Summary

Migrate `Deployment.Spec.Selector` and `ReplicaSet.Spec.Selector` from imperative `ValidateImmutableField` calls to declarative `+k8s:immutable` validation tags, as part of the declarative validation migration ([KEP-5073](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5073)).

- Add `+k8s:immutable` tags to Selector fields across all served API versions (apps/v1, apps/v1beta1, apps/v1beta2, extensions/v1beta1)
- Bootstrap validation-gen for the `apps/v1` internal package
- Mark imperative validation as `.MarkCoveredByDeclarative()` and integrate `rest.ValidateDeclarativelyWithMigrationChecks()` in Deployment and ReplicaSet strategies
- Add declarative validation equivalence tests covering create, update, and immutable selector scenarios with cross-version verification

Part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136785

## Changes

### API type tags (`staging/src/k8s.io/api/`)
- `apps/v1/types.go`: Add `+k8s:required` and `+k8s:immutable` to `DeploymentSpec.Selector` and `ReplicaSetSpec.Selector`
- `apps/v1beta1/types.go`: Add `+k8s:optional` and `+k8s:immutable` to `DeploymentSpec.Selector` (optional in v1beta1)
- `apps/v1beta2/types.go`: Add `+k8s:required` and `+k8s:immutable` to both Selector fields
- `extensions/v1beta1/types.go`: Add `+k8s:optional` and `+k8s:immutable` to both Selector fields

### Validation-gen bootstrap and generated code
- `pkg/apis/apps/v1/doc.go`: Add `+k8s:validation-gen` markers to bootstrap apps/v1
- `pkg/apis/apps/v1/zz_generated.validations.go`: **New** — generated validation for Deployment and ReplicaSet
- `pkg/apis/apps/v1beta1/zz_generated.validations.go`: Updated — add Deployment Selector immutable validation
- `pkg/apis/apps/v1beta2/zz_generated.validations.go`: Updated — add Deployment + ReplicaSet Selector immutable validation
- `staging/.../extensions/v1beta1/zz_generated.validations.go`: Updated — add Deployment + ReplicaSet Selector immutable validation

### Imperative validation integration
- `pkg/apis/apps/validation/validation.go`: Mark imperative `ValidateImmutableField` and required checks with `.MarkCoveredByDeclarative()`
- `pkg/registry/apps/deployment/strategy.go`: Integrate `rest.ValidateDeclarativelyWithMigrationChecks()` in `Validate` and `ValidateUpdate`
- `pkg/registry/apps/replicaset/strategy.go`: Same integration

### Tests
- `pkg/registry/apps/deployment/declarative_validation_test.go`: **New** — DV equivalence tests (create + update + immutable selector)
- `pkg/registry/apps/replicaset/declarative_validation_test.go`: **New** — DV equivalence tests (create + update + immutable selector)
- `pkg/registry/apps/deployment/strategy_test.go`: Update expected error metadata (`Origin`, `CoveredByDeclarative`, `FromImperative`)
- `pkg/registry/apps/replicaset/strategy_test.go`: Same updates

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./pkg/registry/apps/replicaset/...` — all pass
- [x] `go test ./pkg/apis/apps/validation/...` — all pass

title: Label FeatureGate-only e2e tests with proper Feature labels
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/kind failing-test

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The `ci-cri-containerd-node-e2e-unlabelled` job is timing out because tests that
should be categorized under `[Feature:X]` are slipping through the skip regex.

The skip regex uses `[Feature:.+]` to exclude feature tests, but
`framework.WithFeatureGate()` produces `[FeatureGate:X]` in test names — not
`[Feature:X]`. When these feature gates graduated to Beta (default=true) in 1.36,
the tests started actually executing instead of self-skipping at runtime, landing
~53 extra tests (many of them pod resize table entries) in the unlabelled job with
`--nodes=1`, causing the 300m timeout.

The established pattern is to use **both** `feature.X` (for job routing via
`[Feature:X]` text) and `WithFeatureGate(features.Y)` (for runtime semantics).
This is already done by CPUManager, MemoryManager, DRA, HugePages,
ContainerStopSignals, EnvFiles, etc. The tests fixed here were missing the
`feature.X` half.

**Changes:**
- Add `feature.InPlacePodVerticalScaling` to `pod_level_resources_resize.go` and
  `pod_resize.go` (init container SIGDescribe)
- Add `feature.ContainerRestartRules` to both SIGDescribe blocks in
  `container_restart_policy.go`
- Add `feature.DevicePlugin` to `device_plugin_failures_pod_status_test.go`

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The root cause is a mismatch between `[FeatureGate:X]` (produced by
`WithFeatureGate`) and `[Feature:X]` (what job regexes match). This is not a new
pattern — 10+ existing test suites already use both decorators together. The 4
files changed here were simply missing the `feature.X` decorator.

/sig node
/area test
/priority important-soon

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-containerd#node-e2e-unlabelled

The job keeps hitting timeouts.

title: [kubelet] DRA PrepareDynamicResources failures should be reported in SyncResult
body:
## Summary

PrepareDynamicResources failures were not being propagated in the PodSyncResult, causing retries to use the default sync interval (60s-90s) instead of the error backoff path. This significantly increases pod startup latency when PrepareDynamicResources calls fail.

## Changes

- Added `ErrPrepareDynamicResources` error type in sync_result.go
- Added `PrepareDynamicResources` SyncAction constant
- Created a SyncResult for PrepareDynamicResources in SyncPod that captures failures
- Updated test expectations to reflect that PrepareDynamicResources failures are now properly reported

## Impact

When PrepareDynamicResources fails, the pod will now be retried via the error backoff path instead of waiting for the default sync interval, significantly improving pod startup latency in DRA failure scenarios.

Fixes #139836

```release-note
Fixed a bug where the kubelet did not report DynamicResourceAllocation PrepareDynamicResources failures in the pod sync result, causing affected pods to retry on the default resync interval instead of the faster error-backoff path.
```

title: Migrate PV VolumeMode to declarative immutable validation
body:
## What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

## What this PR does / why we need it

Migrates `PersistentVolume.Spec.VolumeMode` immutable field validation from imperative to declarative validation using the `+k8s:immutable` tag. This is part of the KEP-5073 effort to migrate imperative validation to declarative validation.

**Note:** `PersistentVolumeClaim.Spec.VolumeMode` is intentionally excluded from this PR. PVCSpec is transitively embedded in PodTemplateSpec through `EphemeralVolumeSource`, which causes validation-gen to cascade validation to `extensions/v1beta1` staging types that cannot import from `k8s.io/kubernetes`. PVC VolumeMode will be addressed separately once validation-gen supports cross-module boundaries.

## Which issue(s) this PR is related to

Ref: #136785

## Changes

- Add `+k8s:alpha(since: "1.36")=+k8s:immutable` and `+k8s:alpha(since: "1.36")=+k8s:optional` markers to `PersistentVolumeSpec.VolumeMode`
- Add `+k8s:alpha(since: "1.36")=+k8s:optional` to `VolumeAttachmentSource.InlineVolumeSpec` across storage/v1, v1alpha1, v1beta1 for codegen lint compliance
- Mark imperative `ValidateImmutableField` call for PV VolumeMode with `.WithOrigin("immutable").MarkCoveredByDeclarative()`
- Correct VolumeMode field path from `"volumeMode"` to `"spec", "volumeMode"`
- Wrap PV strategy `Validate`/`ValidateUpdate` with `rest.ValidateDeclarativelyWithMigrationChecks`
- Regenerate `zz_generated.validations.go` across affected packages (core/v1, storage/v1, v1alpha1, v1beta1)
- Add declarative validation equivalence test for PV

## Special notes for your reviewer

- Only PV VolumeMode is migrated; PVC VolumeMode remains imperative due to validation-gen cross-module cascade limitation
- The field path correction (`"volumeMode"` → `"spec", "volumeMode"`) aligns the imperative validation error path with the DV-generated path

title: Migrate Node.Spec.ProviderID to declarative set-once validation
body:
## What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

## What this PR does / why we need it

Migrates `Node.Spec.ProviderID` set-once validation from imperative to declarative validation using `+k8s:update=NoModify` and `+k8s:update=NoUnset` tags. ProviderID has set-once semantics: it can be set from empty to a value, but once set cannot be modified or cleared. This is part of the KEP-5073 effort to migrate imperative validation to declarative validation.

## Which issue(s) this PR is related to

Ref: #136785

## Changes

- Add `+k8s:alpha(since: "1.36")=+k8s:update=NoModify` and `+k8s:update=NoUnset` markers to `NodeSpec.ProviderID`
- Split imperative `field.Forbidden` check into two `field.Invalid` checks matching DV error format:
  - `"field cannot be modified once set"` (NoModify) with `.WithOrigin("update").MarkCoveredByDeclarative()`
  - `"field cannot be cleared once set"` (NoUnset) with `.WithOrigin("update").MarkCoveredByDeclarative()`
- Wrap Node strategy `Validate`/`ValidateUpdate` with `rest.ValidateDeclarativelyWithMigrationChecks`
- Regenerate `zz_generated.validations.go`
- Add declarative validation equivalence tests covering set, modify, and clear scenarios

## Special notes for your reviewer

- This is the first use of `+k8s:update=NoModify` + `+k8s:update=NoUnset` for set-once fields in `core/v1`. The only existing `+k8s:update` usage is in the resource API (`ResourceClaim.Status.Allocation` uses `NoModify` alone).
- The `+k8s:update` tag combination `NoModify + NoUnset` correctly implements set-once semantics:
  - `empty → set`: ALLOWED (neither constraint triggers)
  - `set → different`: BLOCKED (NoModify)
  - `set → empty`: BLOCKED (NoUnset)
  - `set → same`: ALLOWED (ratcheting skips unchanged values)
- The imperative error type changed from `field.Forbidden` to `field.Invalid` to match the DV-generated error format. This is an alpha-gated change.

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

title: Fixes : Ephemeral volumes cannot be reclaimed when Pod unadmitted by Kubelet
body:
fix(ephemeral-volume): introduce PodRejected condition and ephemeral controller to clean orphan inline PVCs
When a Pod is rejected during admission or scheduling before being scheduled
to any node, inline ephemeral volume PVCs may become orphaned and never garbage
collected by kubelet.

1. Add PodRejected PodConditionType to mark pods rejected in admission/scheduling phase
2. Kubelet sets PodRejected=True condition when pod is rejected and marks phase Failed
3. Add helper util PodIsRejectedFinished to identify rejected terminated pods
4. Implement ephemeral controller to watch rejected pods and delete orphan ephemeral PVCs
5. Skip PVC creation upfront if pod has already been rejected
6. Update RBAC bootstrap policy for ephemeral controller permissions
7. Adapt pvc protection controller to allow cleanup for rejected pod PVCs

Fixes # 123592

<!--

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change

/kind flake
/kind regression
-->
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Adds observability for the apiserver's watch event delivery pipeline so operators can detect, alert on, and triage watch latency without enabling verbose logging. Currently, attribution of watch slowness is split between blockLogger (etcd3-side, log-only) and ad-hoc symptoms. There's no SLI to alert on, and no decomposition of which stage (cacher, fan-out, watcher, client) is the bottleneck.

This PR introduces the missing metric layer plus a rate-limited per-event diagnostic log.

The SLI:
- `apiserver_watch_cache_dispatch_duration_seconds{group,resource,outcome}` (histogram) - cacher-side dispatch latency ReceivedFromStorageAt → SentToResultChanAt, split by outcome={delivered,terminated} so force-closed watchers' tail stays visible

Per-stage decomposition:
- `apiserver_watcher_queue_duration_seconds{group,resource}` (histogram) - dwell in a specific watcher's input channel. Mild watcher slowness signal
- `apiserver_watcher_dispatch_blocked_seconds_total{group,resource}` (counter) - cumulative seconds the dispatcher was blocked pushing into a watcher's input channel. Signals "this slow watcher is hurting the shared dispatcher."
- `apiserver_watch_cache_queue_duration_seconds{group,resource}` (histogram) - dwell in the cacher's incoming channel before fan-out. Observed once per event; surfaces "cacher itself is the bottleneck."
- `apiserver_watcher_handoff_blocked_seconds_total{group,resource}` (counter) - cumulative seconds a watcher was blocked sending events to its result channel. Signals "The client is consuming events slowly."

Diagnostic log:
- Slow watch cache processing: rate-limited to one line per second process-wide, per-event lifecycle breakdown (cacheAdmitMs, awaitingDispatchMs, dispatchToWatcherMs, awaitingWatcherMs, eventBuildMs, handoffMs)

Triage chain this enables:
p99(dispatch_duration_seconds{outcome="delivered"}) high
   |
   |── watch_cache_queue_duration_seconds rising   → cacher itself behind (pre fan-out)
   |── watcher_dispatch_blocked rate rising                 → slow watcher hurting dispatcher
   |── watcher_queue_duration p99 rising                    → mild watcher buffering
   |── watcher_handoff_blocked rate rising                  → slow client backpressure
   |── (slow-log)                                                               → concrete per-event timeline

title: Export `validateAffinity()` as `ValidateAffinity()` for external validation consistency
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/kind api-change

#### What this PR does / why we need it

The `validateAffinity()` function in the `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/apis/core/validation` package was previously unexported (private). This forced external projects needing to validate Affinity configurations to duplicate approximately 200 lines of validation logic, including helper functions like `validateNodeAffinity`, `validatePodAffinity`, and `validatePodAntiAffinity`.

This PR exports `validateAffinity()` as `ValidateAffinity()`, following the established pattern in the same package where validation methods are already exported for NodeSelector (`ValidateNodeSelector`) and Tolerations (`ValidateTolerations`).

**Benefits:**

- **Reduces Maintenance Burden:** External projects no longer need to keep duplicated logic in sync with upstream changes.
- **Ensures Validation Consistency:** Guarantees that client-side and server-side validation logic remains identical.
- **Follows Project Patterns:** Mirrors the implementation of other exported validation helpers.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to

Fixes #136422

#### Special notes for your reviewer

This is a non-breaking wrapper implementing the suggested approach:

```go
func ValidateAffinity(affinity *core.Affinity, opts PodValidationOptions, fldPath *field.Path) field.ErrorList {
    return validateAffinity(affinity, opts, fldPath)
}
```

Existing internal code paths remain unaffected.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

NONE

N/A

title: Enable declarative validation for Binding resource
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature /kind api-change /sig node /sig api-machinery


#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR enables declarative validation for the Bindingresource as part of the Umbrella issue: Enable Declarative Validation for APIs.

Key changes:
- Adds CEL-based validation rules to the Binding struct in both versioned and internal types.
- Implements a dedicated bindingStrategy in pkg/registry/core/pod/strategy.go, addressing a long-standing TODO in the codebase.
- Refactors BindingREST in pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/storage.go to utilize the new strategy and the declarative validation framework via `rest.ValidateDeclarativelyWithMigrationChecks`.
- Marks manual validation errors in pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Refers to #134280

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
- **CEL Rule Placement**: Specifically placed CEL rules on the Binding struct instead of adding tags to the ObjectReference fields. This was done because ObjectReference is a widely shared type, and adding tags there would have side effects on other resources (like Event or Service) that use it.
- **Stability Markers**: Added `.MarkAlpha()` to the legacy validation errors to satisfy the requirements of `VerifyValidationEquivalence` tests, ensuring the stability levels match exactly.
- **Strategy Implementation**: The implementation of bindingStrategy follows the pattern of other pod subresources (Status, EphemeralContainers) and helps clean up the storage implementation.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Enabled declarative validation for the Binding resource.
```

- Umbrella Issue: #134280

title: kubelet: source OOM events in-tree and drop the cadvisor oomparser dependency
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/kind dependency

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The kubelet used cadvisor's `lib/utils/oomparser` to watch the kernel log for OOM kills and to produce the `container_oom_events_total` metric. This PR moves that work into the kubelet so it no longer depends on the cadvisor lib module for OOM handling.

- The kubelet reads OOM events from `/dev/kmsg` using a forked copy of go-kmsg-parser under `third_party/forked/go-kmsg-parser`. The fork tracks go-kmsg-parser v3 and uses klog for logging.
- The `container_oom_events_total` metric is now generated by the kubelet OOM watcher.
- cadvisor/lib is bumped to v0.60.3. That release no longer ships the OOM parser, so the old `github.com/euank/go-kmsg-parser v2.0.0+incompatible` dependency and the vendored `cadvisor/lib/utils/oomparser` package are removed from the tree.

Behavior is unchanged. OOM events are still emitted and the metric still reports the same counts.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The companion cadvisor change that slims down the lib module is google/cadvisor#3902.

title: Deferred Pod Admission for Unregistered Device Plugins
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we negenerteed it:

When a pod admission fails because a device plugin hasn't registered yet, defer the pod (instead of rejecting it permanently) and retry until either the device plugin registers or a timeout expires. No changes to the device plugin interface.

Replaces https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137919

e2e run: ` make test-e2e-node TEST_ARGS='--kubelet-flags="--fail-swap-on=false"' SKIP= FOCUS="Device Plugin Failures"`

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/125579

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I was experimenting with different placement of retry. I think this is better than inside allocation manager as resize retries are.

Also one of the goals was to minimize the change for the potential possibility to back port to earlier versions, where it may be more important since by the time 1.37 widely adopted, I hope DRA will be more widespread.

I also think long term we may need to have a better accounting of deferred pods so new pods are not admitted in their place. This fix is relying on scheduler to not overcommit. 

Some AI was used

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Defer Pod Admission for the predefined amount of time when the Device Plugin was not registered yet.

title: Pod Certificates: Node-restriction support for signer names
body:
Kubelet's ability to generate service account tokens is restricted by the noderestriction admission plugin, which checks to make sure that the relevant pod actually mounts a token volume with the requested audience.

This commit adds an analogous mechanism for Pod Certificates, restricting the signer names that Kubelet can request.

The feature includes a similar authorizer-based override, where granting the "request-podcertificate-signer" verb for a given signer name allows bypassing the restriction.

Prepared with Claude Code.



/kind bug
/kind api-change

```release-note
The NodeRestriction admission plugin now adds a defense-in-depth check for PodCertificateRequests.  A node may only create a PodCertificateRequest referring to a particular signer name if the pod actually mounts a podCertificate projected volume source that refers to that signer name, or if an authorization check for the user (verb=request-podcertificate-signer resource=<signerName>) succeeds.
```

title: fix: pod-level cgroup was not updated when the OOMKilled container restarts
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Issue description:
when the OOMKilled container restarts, the kubelet calls startContainer. the new container is launched by the CRI runtime using the resource spec from the last known actuatedState, which was never updated. 
so the container starts with the old (too-low) memory limit, hits the old cgroup constraint, and OOMs again.

Fix method:
we cannot call UpdateContainerResources via CRI for non-running container. set UpdatePodResources as true so that doPodResizeAction updates the pod-level cgroup before the container restarts.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fix issue: #138760

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixed a bug in the `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` feature where applying an in-place memory resize while a container was OOMKilled caused the container to keep being OOMKilled on every restart, because the pod-level cgroup `memory.max` was not updated before the container restarted. 
```

title: Fix MAP JSONPatch panic when value is a list of Object literals
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`ObjectVal.ConvertToNative`, when asked for `*structpb.Value`, returns a `*structpb.Struct`. The direct caller in `json_patch.go` tolerates this because it immediately JSON-marshals the result, and a `*structpb.Struct` and a `*structpb.Value` wrapping it serialize identically.

When a MutatingAdmissionPolicy JSONPatch `value` is a list of `Object{}` literals, however, the conversion goes through cel-go's `baseList.ConvertToNative`, which builds a `[]*structpb.Value` via `reflect.Set` on each element. Assigning the `*structpb.Struct` into a `*structpb.Value` slice slot panics, and the panic propagates through the admission chain to the request handler, so the client sees `stream error: INTERNAL_ERROR; received from peer` rather than a policy error. `failurePolicy: Ignore` does not suppress it because the panic unwinds past the dispatcher's error collection.

Apiserver log signature:

```
"APIServer panic'd: reflect.Set: value of type *structpb.Struct is not assignable to type *structpb.Value"
```

This PR wraps the struct in `structpb.NewStructValue` so the declared return type is honored. A unit test asserts the returned type, and a `TestJSONPatch` table case covers the list-of-initializers shape that triggered the panic; that case panics with the trace above on an unpatched tree.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3962

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The bug has existed since the `ObjectVal` introduction in 9ee1ea9d37c2 and is present in 1.32 through current master. A separate hardening change to have the mutating dispatcher recover from CEL evaluation panics and route them through `failurePolicy` would be worthwhile but is not included here.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a kube-apiserver panic when a MutatingAdmissionPolicy JSONPatch expression sets `value` to a list of `Object{}` literals.
```

title: KEP-6063: Support per-pod PID limits via resources.limits.pid (Alpha)
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature
/kind api-change

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Implements [KEP-6063](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6064), adding support for per-pod PID limits via `spec.resources.limits.pid`,
using the pod-level resource API. This allows workload authors to set a single PID limit
shared by all containers in a pod, independent of the node-level `--pod-pids-limit` kubelet
flag. The effective limit is enforced as `min(node podPidsLimit, pod spec.resources.limits.pid)`,
ensuring pods cannot exceed the node administrator's ceiling.

Changes include:

- `PerPodPIDLimit` feature gate (Alpha, v1.37, disabled by default)
- `PerPodPIDLimit` depends on `PodLevelResources` feature gate (Beta, enabled by default since v1.34). If `PodLevelResources` is disabled, `PerPodPIDLimit` cannot be enabled.
- `ResourcePID` constant registered as a standard, integer, non-overcommittable resource
- API validation enforcing range 1024–16384 at the pod level
- `pid` rejected at container level (pod-level only resource)
- Field stripping when gate is disabled, preserving existing pods
- Kubelet enforcement on cgroupsv2; pods specifying pid are rejected on cgroupsv1 nodes during admission
- PIDLimitCapped warning event emitted when a pod's requested PID limit is capped by the node's podPidsLimit
- Prometheus metric `kubelet_pod_pid_limit_applied_total`
- Node Declared Features integration: kubelet declares `PerPodPIDLimit` in `node.status.declaredFeatures` when the feature gate is enabled and cgroupsv2 is available, enabling the scheduler to filter incompatible nodes
- Unit tests (34 cases) and e2e node tests (4 cases)

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Enhancements: kubernetes/enhancements#6063
KEP: kubernetes/enhancements#6064

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- The feature is gated behind `PerPodPIDLimit` (Alpha, disabled by default), so no impact on existing behavior.
- `PerPodPIDLimit` declares `PodLevelResources` as a dependency in the feature gate dependency map. If someone disables `PodLevelResources`, `PerPodPIDLimit` will be rejected at startup.
- PID limit is specified at the pod level (`spec.resources.limits.pid`), not at the container level. All containers in the pod share a single PID pool.
- Per-pod PID limits require cgroupsv2. On cgroupsv1 nodes, the kubelet rejects pods that specify `spec.resources.limits.pid` during admission, preventing silent non-enforcement.
- When the effective PID limit is capped by the node's podPidsLimit, the kubelet emits a PIDLimitCapped warning event on the pod (visible via kubectl describe pod).
- `pid` is non-overcommittable: requests must equal limits.
- Pod Security Admission (PSA): the pid resource field has no PSA impact — pods are admitted under all PSA profiles (Privileged, Baseline, Restricted).
- Node Declared Features: the kubelet declares `PerPodPIDLimit` in `node.status.declaredFeatures` when the gate is enabled and the node runs cgroupsv2. The scheduler infers that pods with `spec.resources.limits.pid` require this feature and avoids scheduling them on incompatible nodes.
- `hostPID: true` is fully compatible with per-pod PID limits. PID namespace (process visibility) and PID cgroup controller (process creation accounting) are independent kernel subsystems — host processes are visible but not counted against the pod's PID limit.
- E2e node tests require a cgroupsv2 environment to run.

### Testing
**Unit Tests (49 cases):**
- API validation: pid range (1024–16384), container-level rejection, non-overcommittable enforcement, zero/negative values
- Feature gate interaction: field stripping when PerPodPIDLimit disabled, PodLevelResources dependency
- Kubelet: getPodPIDLimit logic (pod limit lower/higher than node, no pod limit fallback)
- Helpers: ResourcePID not in standardContainerResources, overcommit not allowed
- Kubelet: cgroupsv1 rejection error message validation
- Kubelet: PIDLimitCapped event emission when capped, no event when not capped
- Eviction: PID pressure detection and eviction ranking unaffected by per-pod PID limits
- Node Declared Features: PerPodPIDLimit feature requirements, discovery (gate enabled/disabled × cgroupsv2/v1), scheduling inference (with/without PID limits), update inference, registry consistency


**E2E Node Tests (6 automated cases):**

1. Pod PID limit lower than node default → pod limit applied
2. Pod PID limit higher than node default → capped at node default
3. Multi-container pod shares single pod-level PID limit
4. No pod PID limit → fallback to node default
5. Pod with hostPID=true and pid=1024 → pids.max=1024 enforced in pod cgroup despite shared PID namespace; host processes visible via ps but not counted against limit; fork fails with "Resource temporarily unavailable" at 1024
6. Pod with pid limit admitted under Baseline PSA profile and limit enforced
7. Pod with pid limit admitted under Restricted PSA profile and limit enforced

**Manual E2E Verification (Kind cluster, cgroupsv2, podPidsLimit=4096):**
All 12 scenarios passed:
1. pid=1024 (lower than node 4096) → pod cgroup pids.max=1024
2. pid=8192 (higher than node 4096) → capped at pids.max=4096 + PIDLimitCapped event emitted
3. Multi-container pod pid=2048 → shared pod-level pids.max=2048
4. No pid limit → fallback pids.max=4096 (node default)
5. pid=100 (below min 1024) → API rejection
6. pid=20000 (above max 16384) → API rejection
7. requests.pid specified → silently stripped, only limits.pid preserved
8. Fork bomb enforcement: processes spawn up to ~1024, then `can't fork: Resource temporarily unavailable`
9. Pod with hostPID=true and pid=1024 → pids.max=1024 enforced in pod cgroup despite shared PID namespace; host processes visible via ps but not counted against limit; fork fails with "Resource temporarily unavailable" at 1024
10. PSA Baseline and Restricted: pods with PID limit admitted
11. Node Declared Features: `node.status.declaredFeatures` contains `PerPodPIDLimit`
12. Static pod with pid=2048 → pod cgroup pids.max=2048 (bypasses apiserver)

#### Manual verification - Test 1 (Pod PID limit lower than node default)

- Verify node-level podPidsLimit
```
$ kubectl get --raw /api/v1/nodes/pid-limit-test-control-plane/proxy/configz | python3 -c "import sys,json; cfg=json.load(sys.stdin)['kubeletconfig']; print('podPidsLimit:', cfg.get('podPidsLimit'))"
podPidsLimit: 4096
```
- Create pod with pid=2048 (lower than node default 4096)
```
$ cat test1-pid-lower.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test1-pid-lower
spec:
  resources:
    limits:
      pid: "2048"
    requests:
      pid: "2048"
  containers:
    - name: test-container
      image: busybox
      command: ["sleep", "3600"]
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "10m"
          memory: "100Mi"
$ kubectl apply -f test1-pid-lower.yaml
pod/test1-pid-lower created
$ kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/test1-pid-lower --timeout=60s
pod/test1-pid-lower condition met
$ kubectl get pod test1-pid-lower -o wide
NAME              READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP           NODE                           NOMINATED NODE   READINESS GATES
test1-pid-lower   1/1     Running   0          15s   10.244.0.6   pid-limit-test-control-plane   <none>           <none>
```
- Verify pids.max at pod-level cgroup
```
$ POD_UID=$(kubectl get pod test1-pid-lower -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')
$ podman exec pid-limit-test-control-plane cat /sys/fs/cgroup/kubelet.slice/kubelet-kubepods.slice/kubelet-kubepods-burstable.slice/kubelet-kubepods-burstable-pod${POD_UID//-/_}.slice/pids.max
2048
```
- Pod requested pid=2048, node podPidsLimit=4096
- Effective limit = min(4096, 2048) = 2048. Confirmed via pod-level cgroup pids.max.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Add support for per-pod PID limits via spec.resources.limits.pid, gated behind the PerPodPIDLimit feature gate (Alpha, disabled by default). This feature depends on `PodLevelResources` (Beta, enabled by default since v1.34). When enabled on cgroupsv2 nodes, the kubelet enforces the effective PID limit as min(node podPidsLimit, pod spec.resources.limits.pid). On cgroupsv1 nodes, pods specifying pid limits are rejected during admission. All containers in the pod share a single PID pool. The kubelet declares `PerPodPIDLimit` in node.status.declaredFeatures, enabling the scheduler to avoid placing PID-limited pods on incompatible nodes.
```
/sig node
/cc @haircommander @ngopalak-redhat

body:

5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?

<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug
/kind dependency
/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

On nodes with hugepages configured, the kubelet's `memory.available` eviction signal overstates real available regular memory by the total hugepage reservation. This causes eviction to fire later than the configured threshold intends, leading to OOM kills.
The root cause is that `AvailableBytes` is computed as `limit - workingSet`, where:
- `limit` is set to `MemTotal` from `/proc/meminfo` (includes hugepage-reserved RAM)
- `workingSet` comes from the memory cgroup controller (does not track hugetlb allocations — those use a separate controller)
This creates "phantom" available bytes equal to the hugepage reservation. The kernel's own `MemAvailable` in `/proc/meminfo` does not have this problem because hugepage-reserved pages are removed from the buddy allocator's free pool at boot.

#### How does this PR fix it

Introduces `adjustForHugePages()` in `pkg/kubelet/server/stats/summary.go` that subtracts the node's total hugepage capacity from `AvailableBytes` when constructing `NodeStats.Memory`. This is applied in both `Get()` and `GetCPUAndMemoryStats()`, so the eviction manager sees corrected values without any changes to the eviction logic itself.

The adjustment clamps to zero if hugepage capacity exceeds reported available bytes.

title: Fix eviction grace period
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
When `--eviction-max-pod-grace-period` is set to a negative value, the flag help
text says it should "defer to pod specified value." Instead, the negative value
passes through `min()`, which always picks the negative number over the pod's
`TerminationGracePeriodSeconds`. The CRI runtime interprets the negative value as
immediate termination, causing SIGKILL (exit code 137) instead of a graceful shutdown.

This fix checks for negative values before the `min()` call and uses the pod's
own `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds` directly.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #118172

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
- Fix is in `pkg/kubelet/eviction/eviction_manager.go` (4 lines of logic)
- New test `TestNegativeMaxPodGracePeriodDefersToPodsGracePeriod` verifies the fix
- All existing eviction tests pass

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixed a bug where setting --eviction-max-pod-grace-period to a negative value caused immediate pod termination instead of deferring to the pod's TerminationGracePeriodSeconds.

Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

title: Migrate: use source file permission when writing destination file
body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
If you have a `~/.kube/.kubeconfig` file and no `~/.kube/config` file, client-go will perform a migration, which reads the contents of `~/.kube/.kubeconfig` and writes it to `~/.kube/config`.

However, the newly created `~/.kube/config` file is always created with `0666` permissions (subject to umask), which can result in `~/.kube/config` permissions exceeding `~/.kube/.kubeconfig` permissions as shown in the following example after migration has occurred:

```
~/.kube % umask
022
~/.kube % ls -l .kubeconfig config
-rw-------@ 1 bpursley  staff  5602 Mar 31 10:29 .kubeconfig
-rw-r--r--@ 1 bpursley  staff  5602 Mar 31 10:29 config
```

This can be a problem because config files can contain credentials, and the migration *could in some cases* result in accidental credential exposure to other users on the same system.

This PR changes the migrate functionality to use the source file's permissions when writing the destination file.  It still remains subject to umask as it does currently, so the destination permission may not exactly match the source permission, but with this change, the destination file's permissions won't exceed the source file's permissions.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
N/A

title: e2e_node_windows: add CPU affinity tests
body:
e2e_node_windows: add CPU manager affinity node e2e tests

Add node e2e tests for Windows CPU manager exclusive-CPU affinity
(static policy, WindowsCPUAndMemoryAffinity feature gate), covering how
affinity is applied to containers and how it is verified on Windows.

Tests (cpu_manager_test.go):
- Guaranteed pods get exactly the requested number of exclusive CPUs
  (1/2/3-CPU single-container pods), with non-overlapping CPUs across
  containers in a multi-container pod (1+2, 3+2) and across separate
  guaranteed pods (2+2).
- Non-guaranteed (burstable) containers get no affinity, including a
  burstable pod coexisting with a guaranteed one.
- With the WindowsCPUAndMemoryAffinity feature gate off, guaranteed pods
  get no affinity (negative cases).
- Init containers: a restartable sidecar holds exclusive CPUs separately
  from the app container; the app container gains exclusive CPUs after a
  non-restartable init container completes.

Verification is two-layered:
- CRI read-back of ContainerStatus Windows.AffinityCpus ("containerd
  recorded what the kubelet asked for"), and
- the actual Win32 job-object affinity of the hcsshim container silo
  ("the kernel applied it"), read under brief SYSTEM impersonation since
  the silo job object is accessible only to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

Suite plumbing: drop the dependency on test/e2e_node by porting the
kubeletconfig and criproxy subpackages locally (the CRI proxy uses a
Windows named pipe), plus shared helpers (util*.go) for kubelet config,
Windows service control, CRI/host affinity reads, and SYSTEM
impersonation.

title: Migrate HPA CrossVersionObjectReference.Kind and .Name to declarative validation
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR migrates the `required` validation for `CrossVersionObjectReference.Kind` and `CrossVersionObjectReference.Name` fields to declarative validation (DV) using `+k8s:alpha(since: "1.36")=+k8s:required` tags. This is part of the broader declarative validation migration effort (KEP-5073).

**Changes:**
1. **`staging/src/k8s.io/api/autoscaling/v1/types.go`** and **`v2/types.go`**: Added `+k8s:alpha(since: "1.36")=+k8s:required` to `CrossVersionObjectReference.Kind` and `.Name` fields
2. **`staging/src/k8s.io/api/autoscaling/v2/types.go`**: Added `+k8s:alpha(since: "1.36")=+k8s:optional` to 4 cascading fields that transitively contain `CrossVersionObjectReference` (`HorizontalPodAutoscalerSpec.Metrics`, `MetricSpec.Object`, `HorizontalPodAutoscalerStatus.CurrentMetrics`, `MetricStatus.Object`)
3. **`pkg/apis/autoscaling/validation/validation.go`**: Marked hand-written `Required` checks with `.MarkCoveredByDeclarative()`
4. **`pkg/registry/autoscaling/horizontalpodautoscaler/declarative_validation_test.go`**: Added equivalence test cases for create and update scenarios
5. Regenerated validation (`zz_generated.validations.go`) and protobuf (`generated.proto`) files via `hack/update-codegen.sh`

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/135752

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5073

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

- `CrossVersionObjectReference` is defined separately in both `autoscaling/v1` and `autoscaling/v2` — both are updated.
- Adding `+k8s:required` to `CrossVersionObjectReference` fields triggered cascading DV lint requirements in v2 for fields that transitively contain `CrossVersionObjectReference`. Four already-optional fields needed explicit `+k8s:optional` declarations to satisfy the lint rule.
- The `else` branches of the hand-written validation (which validate `IsPathSegmentName`) are NOT marked as covered by DV, since DV does not yet support that validation. Only the `Required` checks are covered.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

```docs

```

title: Validate node name in Binding API
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The Binding API doesn't validate node names, so you can bind a pod to a node with an invalid name (like uppercase characters). If the pod has a finalizer, it gets stuck in deletion because the node doesn't exist and never will.

This adds validation to `ValidatePodBinding` to reject invalid node names upfront using the existing `ValidateNodeName` function.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #136723

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
The `pods/binding` endpoint now validates the specified node name consistently.
```

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR fixes error reporting for HTTP/TCP liveness, readiness, and startup probes when a probe references a named port that does not exist in the container.

Previously, `ResolveContainerPort` fell back to `strconv.Atoi` for `intstr.String` values after named port lookup failed. For unresolved named ports, that hid the real error behind a parse failure like:

`strconv.Atoi: parsing "metrcis": invalid syntax`

This change:

- removes the `Atoi` fallback from the string branch in `ResolveContainerPort`
- returns a clearer `port "<name>" not found` error for unresolved named ports
- keeps existing probe behavior unchanged (`probe.Unknown`)
- updates tests that relied on numeric ports being passed as strings

This matches API validation more closely because string port names must contain at least one letter, so numeric-string fallback in this path is misleading rather than useful.

**What this does**

The PV, PVC and VAC protection controllers register their informer event
handlers via `AddEventHandler`, which logs through the global
`klog.Background()` logger. This switches them to

`cache.HandlerOptions{Logger: &logger}`, so event-handler logging is
contextual. The registration errors that were previously discarded
(`_, _ =`) are now surfaced with `utilruntime.Must`.

Part of the contextual logging migration tracked in #126379, following
the same pattern as the other `AddEventHandlerWithOptions` controller
migrations.

title: Fix emptyDir teardown failure when Bidirectional mount propagation leaks submounts into volume directory
body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/first-contribution.md#your-first-contribution and developer guide https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/development.md#development-guide
2. Please label this pull request according to what type of issue you are addressing, especially if this is a release targeted pull request. For reference on required PR/issue labels, read here:
https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-release/release.md#issuepr-kind-label
3. Ensure you have added or ran the appropriate tests for your PR: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-testing/testing.md
4. If you want *faster* PR reviews, read how: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#best-practices-for-faster-reviews
5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When `terminationMessagePath` points to a file inside a `Bidirectional` mounted emptyDir volume, deleting the pod gets stuck permanently with `unlinkat ... device or resource busy`.

This happens because the termination message file is bind mounted into the container at a path within the Bidirectional volume. Due to `MS_SHARED` propagation, that bind mount propagates back to the host, making the file inside the emptyDir host path a mount point. When the volume manager tries to tear down the emptyDir via `os.RemoveAll`, it fails with `EBUSY` because you cannot unlink a mount point.

This PR adds an `unmountSubmounts` step to both `teardownDefault()` and `teardownTmpfsOrHugetlbfs()` in the emptyDir volume plugin. Before removing or unmounting the volume directory, it lists all mount points, finds any that are within the emptyDir directory, and unmounts them in reverse order (deepest first). This makes emptyDir teardown resilient to stale mounts left behind by Bidirectional mount propagation.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #115054

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The root cause was identified in the issue discussion by @smarterclayton ([comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115054#issuecomment-1402493377)) and me ([comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115054#issuecomment-1409209266), [comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115054#issuecomment-1402351442)):
- The termination message file is bind-mounted into the container at the `terminationMessagePath` (e.g. `/cache/log.txt`)
- Because `/cache` uses `mountPropagation: Bidirectional`, the bind mount propagates back to the host mount namespace
- When the container is removed, the propagated mount on the host persists
- `os.RemoveAll` on the emptyDir directory fails because the file is still a mount point

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed a bug where pods using `terminationMessagePath` pointing to a file inside a Bidirectional-mounted emptyDir volume would get stuck in Terminating state. The emptyDir teardown now correctly unmounts any propagated submounts before removing the volume directory.
```

```docs

```

title: kube-proxy: detect host CPU count via cpuset.NumCPU instead of cadvisor
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

kube-proxy sizes `nf_conntrack_max` from the node's CPU count. It used to get that count from cadvisor, through the `github.com/google/cadvisor/lib` machine topology. This change drops that cadvisor dependency from `pkg/proxy/conntrack` and uses `cpuset.NumCPU()` from `k8s.io/utils` instead.

`nf_conntrack_max` is a host-wide setting, so it has to be sized from the whole node's CPU count. `runtime.NumCPU()` is not right for this, because it follows the process cpuset and returns a smaller number when kube-proxy runs under a static CPU policy. `cpuset.NumCPU()` reads the online CPU count from `/sys/devices/system/cpu/online`, which the cpuset does not affect. The code falls back to `runtime.NumCPU()` if that file cannot be read.

`cpuset.NumCPU()` was added to `k8s.io/utils` in kubernetes/utils#354, so this PR also bumps `k8s.io/utils` to pick it up.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Related to #99225

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

`detectNumCPU` is now `cpuset.NumCPU()` with a `runtime.NumCPU()` fallback. This also addresses the earlier review comments about reading the right file, the comment wording, and moving the helper into `cpuset`.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

NONE
```

title: Feature/pod group as victim
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR enhances the standard Pod-by-Pod preemption flow to support PodGroups as preemption victims. Previously, the preemption logic treated all pods individually. With this change, if a pod belongs to a PodGroup, the preemption logic can treat the group as a single atomic victim.

High-level overview of how this was achieved:
- **Interface Abstraction**: Introduced `Victim` and `DomainVictim` separation.
    - **`Victim`**: A general type used to generalize single Pods and `PodGroups`. It supports operations that do not depend on a specific preemption domain.
    - **`DomainVictim`**: Tied strictly to a preemption domain. It tracks `nodeInfos` (copies of node state, not active snapshot references, except WAP flow, for WAP we are using actual reference) representing the affected blast radius, which the preemption algorithm uses to identify pods for eviction. It cannot be created outside of a domain.
- **Constructor Methods**:
    - `NewVictim` signature was updated to return the `Victim` interface and made public.
    - Added `NewDomainForPodByPodPreemption` which initializes the preemption domain by grouping pods on a node by their `PodGroupName` (if applicable).
    - The `DomainVictim` constructor (`newDomainVictim`) calculates `nodeInfos` internally using a snapshot reference, rather than requiring them to be passed from outside the domain.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
The changes focus on abstracting the "unit of preemption" into a `Victim` interface. The `NewDomainForPodByPodPreemption` constructor is where the grouping logic lives.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Enhanced Pod-by-Pod preemption to support PodGroups as preemption victims.
```

title: apiserver: add configurable HTTP/2 write and read-idle timeouts
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Right now kube-apiserver has no connection-level write timeout. If an HTTP/2
client stops reading the response (its receive buffer fills up and stays full),
the server's `writeDataFromHandler` goroutine just parks in a `select` waiting
for flow-control credit that never comes. There's no `<-ctx.Done()` case in that
select, so the 60s cancellation from the `WithTimeoutForNonLongRunningRequests`
filter never gets observed. The goroutine holds onto its APF seat until the TCP
connection finally dies on its own, which can take a long time.

This is the server side of #111886. It isn't really client specific either, any
HTTP/2 client whose body reader can stall will do it (slow consumer, killed
process, a thread that's blocked on something else).

So this adds two flags:

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--http2-write-byte-timeout` | `0` (disabled) | Close the connection if no bytes can be written to it for this long |
| `--http2-read-idle-timeout` | `0` (disabled) | Send a PING after this much idle time, close if there's no PONG |

It also hooks up `http2.Server.CountError` to a new counter
`apiserver_http2_server_errors_total{type}`, mostly so ping timeouts and protocol
violations are actually visible somewhere instead of silently closing conns.

How it behaves:

- Stalled LIST/GET (client recv buffer full): server closes the connection after
  `--http2-write-byte-timeout`, the handler goroutine wakes up and the APF seat
  gets released.
- Normal watch (events flowing, or just quiet): the write timeout doesn't fire.
  `WriteByteTimeout` only runs the timer while a write is actually blocked, and it
  resets as soon as any bytes go out, so an idle watch with nothing pending is
  fine.
- Dead peer (`--http2-read-idle-timeout`): PING goes out after the idle interval,
  and the conn is closed if no PONG comes back within `PingTimeout` (15s default).

Both default to `0`, so nothing changes on an existing cluster unless you opt in.
If you do turn the write timeout on, 60s is a reasonable starting point.

A couple of "why not X" notes since they come up:

`http.Server.WriteTimeout` won't work here. That one is a total per-request write
deadline, so it would kill every watch the moment they hit it.
`http2.Server.WriteByteTimeout` is a different thing, the timer only runs while a
write is in progress and resets on any bytes written, so idle watches aren't
touched.

KEP-4460 (per-request deadline through `ResponseController`) was the other option.
That was tried in #114189 and hit a nil pointer panic in
`net/http.(*http2pipe).CloseWithError`. The underlying Go bug
(golang/go#65526, the HTTP/1.x handler hang with `SetWriteDeadline`) has been open
since early 2024 with no movement. `WriteByteTimeout` sits at the connection layer
underneath `ResponseController` so it sidesteps that whole thing.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Fixes #111886

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Tests added:

- `TestSecureServingOptionsHTTP2Timeouts` (`pkg/server/options/serving_test.go`):
  checks the two flags default to `0`, parse, and make it through `ApplyTo` into
  `SecureServingInfo`.
- `TestSecureServingWriteByteTimeoutDoesNotAffectStreamingResponses`
  (`pkg/server/secure_serving_test.go`): runs the real `SecureServingInfo.Serve`
  path with `HTTP2WriteByteTimeout` set, and checks that a watch-style streaming
  response with idle gaps longer than the timeout doesn't get closed. Basically
  the "we didn't break watches" guarantee.

One thing I left out on purpose: there's no test asserting the timeout actually
fires on a stalled reader, and none for the read-idle ping timeout. To trigger
either of those deterministically you need a hand-rolled `http2.Framer` client
that advertises a big flow-control window but then stops draining the socket (for
the write timeout) or ignores PINGs (for read-idle), and you end up racing real
kernel socket buffers. x/net/http2 only tests these with its own internal fake
clock, which we can't get at from here. So those tests would be flaky and would
mostly be re-testing x/net behavior rather than anything this PR does. Can add
them if you'd rather have them, just didn't want to ship something flaky.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kube-apiserver: added two new flags, `--http2-write-byte-timeout` and `--http2-read-idle-timeout`, to configure server-side HTTP/2 connection timeouts. `--http2-write-byte-timeout` closes a connection when the server has been unable to write response bytes for the configured duration (for example, a stalled client whose receive buffer is full), which releases the API Priority and Fairness seat held by the blocked request handler. `--http2-read-idle-timeout` sends an HTTP/2 PING after the configured period with no incoming frames and closes the connection if no response is received. Both flags default to `0` (disabled), so there is no change in behavior unless they are set. A new metric `apiserver_http2_server_errors_total` was also added to make HTTP/2 server errors and ping timeouts observable.
```

```docs

```

title: volume: use AddEventHandlerWithOptions in more controllers
body:
**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The attachdetach, expand, ephemeral, selinuxwarning and persistentvolume
controllers registered their informer event handlers via `AddEventHandler`,
which logs through the global `klog.Background()` logger. This switches them to
`AddEventHandlerWithOptions` and passes the controller's contextual logger so
event-handler logging is contextual.

For the controllers that previously discarded the registration result, the
returned error is now surfaced via `runtime.Must` instead of being ignored.
`selinuxwarning` already returned the registration error, so its handling is
left as-is.

This is a follow-up to #139943 (the PV/PVC/VAC protection controllers) for the
remaining volume controllers, and is part of the contextual logging migration
tracked in #126379.

No behavior change, so no new tests are added; the existing unit tests for these
packages continue to pass.

Part of #126379

title: Use HandleCrashWithContext in controlplane controllers
body:
Migrate two controlplane controllers to contextual logging by replacing
utilruntime.HandleCrash with utilruntime.HandleCrashWithContext where a
context is already in scope. This lets panic handlers log through the
context bound logger instead of the global background logger, matching the
already migrated apiserverleasegc controller.

Refs kubernetes/kubernetes#126379

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Part of the contextual logging migration. In legacytokentracking and
clusterauthenticationtrust, the panic recovery handler still called the
non contextual utilruntime.HandleCrash() even though a context.Context was
already available in the enclosing function (RunWithContext(ctx) and
Run(ctx, workers) respectively). Switching to
utilruntime.HandleCrashWithContext(ctx) routes panic logging through the
context bound logger instead of klog.Background(), consistent with the
already migrated apiserverleasegc controller. No public signatures change.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

Refs kubernetes/kubernetes#126379

#### Other notes:

Scoped intentionally small: only the two call sites where a context was
already in scope, so the change is signature preserving and low risk. The
systemnamespaces and crdregistration controllers in the same directory
still take only a stop channel and need a RunWithContext variant before
they can be migrated; those are left for a follow up.

Verified with go build, go vet, and the package unit tests for both
controllers.

title: authorization: enable optionalorrequired kube-api-linter rule
body:
Enables the `optionalorrequired` and `nonpointerstructs` kube-api-linter rules for the `authorization` API group. Part of #134671, addresses #136861.

**What:**
- Tags every field in `authorization/v1` and `v1beta1` as `+optional` / `+required`.
- `*.Status` fields are server-populated and optional on input, so they stay `+optional` via a scoped `nonpointerstructs` exception (they can't become pointers without breaking these stable APIs). Happy to mark them `+required` instead if that's preferred — `status` may tighten per API conventions.
- Generated protobuf and OpenAPI specs regenerated; no behavior change.

```release-note
Updated the authorization API group to improve OpenAPI schema correctness for fields being optional or required.
```

/sig auth
/assign @JoelSpeed

title: docs(apimachinery): fix malformed resourceVersion godoc in ObjectMeta
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/sig api-machinery

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The godoc for `ObjectMeta.ResourceVersion` contains a malformed, truncated sentence — `Value must be treated as opaque by clients and .` — which ends mid-clause (`and .`) and duplicates the guidance already stated two lines above ("Clients must treat these values as opaque and passed unmodified back to the server.").

Because the comment is a code-generation source, the broken text is propagated into the derived API documentation: the generated swagger docs, the generated protobuf, the applyconfigurations, the published OpenAPI v2/v3 specs, and several generated/testdata fixtures. This PR removes the malformed line and updates every generated/derived file it had propagated into.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

N/A

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The change only removes the duplicated/truncated sentence; the surrounding wording is unchanged. The diff therefore touches one source comment plus the generated files that mirror it. The vendored historical kustomize OpenAPI snapshot (`vendor/sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/kyaml/openapi/kubernetesapi/v1_21_2/swagger.pb`) is intentionally left untouched.

Disclosure: this change was prepared with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Claude Code); it was reviewed and is submitted by the author.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
NONE
```
